cwe_name: Improper Encoding or Escaping of Output

exact_cwe_mechanism.evidence: The code directly interpolates encoding names and values into HTML without proper escaping, which is the core mechanism of CWE-116 - improper output encoding when generating structured messages (HTML) for communication.

connection.evidence: Encoding names (enc) and values (processed through Utils.printable) are connected to HTML table construction. Utils.printable only handles non-printable characters but does not escape HTML metacharacters.

diff_causality.evidence: This candidate line materially creates the vulnerability by performing the unsafe HTML interpolation. Reverting this line would remove the vulnerable output generation entirely.

security_control.evidence: The required HTML escaping control is missing for encoding names and values.
security_control.required_control: HTML entity encoding for user-controlled data before interpolation into HTML
security_control.control_requirement_evidence: CWE-116 requires proper encoding when outputting data into structured formats like HTML to prevent injection attacks
existing_controls_checked: Utils.printable() only replaces non-printable characters, does not escape HTML metacharacters
No additional HTML escaping is applied before interpolation
security_control.deficiency_evidence: The code directly interpolates encoding data using template literals without any HTML escaping, allowing script injection if encoding names/values contain HTML metacharacters

concrete_impact.evidence: Cross-site scripting (XSS) is possible if encoding names or values contain malicious scripts, though the exact exploitability depends on how encodings data is sourced.

diff_counterfactual: If the candidate line were reverted, the unsafe HTML interpolation would not occur, preventing the improper output encoding vulnerability.
supporting_evidence: Template literal interpolation directly embeds encoding names and values into HTML without escaping
Utils.printable() documentation confirms it only handles non-printable characters, not HTML metacharacters
Method returns HTML content (presentType is 'html') indicating this output is rendered directly
No evidence of additional HTML escaping layer in the code path
unresolved_facts: Whether encoding names from IO_FORMAT are trusted/safe
Whether the application framework provides additional HTML escaping layer
How encodings parameter data is sourced and whether it contains user-controlled content
review_comment: Encoding names and values are directly interpolated into HTML without proper escaping, creating a cross-site scripting vulnerability. The Utils.printable function only handles non-printable characters but does not escape HTML metacharacters. Apply HTML entity encoding to both encoding names and values before interpolation using a dedicated HTML escaping function.
